{"decision":"PROPOSED, NOT TAKEN — this changes what every existing scoped caller sees, so it waits on the owner's word.

THREE PARTS, and they can be answered separately:

(1) `DEFAULT_SCOPE_DEPTH` becomes 2. At 3 the scoped detectors do not narrow: measured over all 56 Components of reflow2's own design, each returns 50-60 of the 83 gaps (median 55) and a region of 595-903 nodes. At 2 the same sweep returns 2-27 (median 4) over regions of 267-601. See `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design`.

(2) The docstring that justifies 3 is corrected whatever is decided about the number. It argues the third hop is needed to reach 'a contained child component's capabilities' — but `scope_region` puts the whole containment closure into the seed set BEFORE taking the radius, so those capabilities are one hop from an owned node, not three. The reason given for the default is not a reason the code needs.

(3) `detect_gaps`' description stops claiming its region is 'the same computation claim_region uses ... so "my area" means one thing everywhere'. It is not: the depths differ (3 vs 2) and `scope_region` adds the containment closure that `claimed_region` omits. Either the sentence goes or the two computations are actually reconciled — and reconciling them changes what two people believe they hold, which is a bigger question than a default.","name":"The default scope depth drops from 3 to 2, and the two definitions of "a region" stop being described as one","rationale":"WHY IT IS PUT RATHER THAN TAKEN, given the standing rule to fix things properly while they are still cheap: the rule is about not patching around a mistake, and none of this is a patch. But a default that every scoped caller already reads is design intent about what 'my part' means, and `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is the reason an agent does not settle that alone. Part (2) is a plain factual correction to a comment and needs nobody's permission; parts (1) and (3) do.

WHAT WAS REJECTED. Leaving the default at 3 and telling callers to pass a depth: the measurement says the default is what almost everyone gets, and a tool whose out-of-the-box answer is 'two thirds of the design, called your part' fails the epoch this sits in. Also rejected: making `design_regions` quietly use a different depth from the scoped detectors, which would have hidden the defect behind a second opinion instead of naming it.

COST OF DECIDING LATER RATHER THAN NOW, stated because the standing rule asks for it: every session that scopes between now and then is told its part holds two thirds of the design's gaps, and any judgement made on that number — 'my area is the messy one' — is made on a figure that is the same for every area.","status":"proposed"}
